docs.title: About Unloaded Activity
docs.text: Unloaded Activity is a Minecraft mod which makes chunks and entities seem like they’re always being simulated, by keeping track of when they were last simulated and then updating them accordingly.

docs.title: THIS WIKI IS A WORK IN PROGRESS
docs.text: My focus is currently on other projects of mine. If you're a developer and want to add support for my mod, please join my Discord server and contact me directly (@kemoono) and I'll help you out!

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: Unloaded Activity makes use of datapacks to know which blocks/blockentities to simulate and how to simulate them. You use datapacks to assign and configure SimulationMethods onto different blocks. If you need more control, you are able to register your own custom SimulationMethods from Java to use inside your datapack.

docs.title: Why datapacks?
docs.text:
For flexibility and (hopefully) easier mod support.

Previously, this mod would use an interface to add custom simulation behavior to blocks. The problem with this would be that if a mod wanted to modify the behavior of vanilla blocks it would have to make a new mixin and override the simulation method implemented by one of this mods mixin and copy over the implementation to then do the needed changes.

Another problem is that if a custom crop changes the probability for crop growth, it would also have to copy and paste the simulation method implementation. This could be made easier by making another method specifically for returning growth probability so it'd only need to override that, but it'd still be a bit annoying.

Additionally, if a mod wanted to have Unloaded Activity be optional for the user, it'd have to register different block classes depending on if Unloaded Activity is present or not. One with the simulation methods overridden, and one without the methods.

With datapacks however, you are able to change different values, vanilla block or not, without much trouble, and without having to check if Unloaded Activity is installed or not.

Here's how data/minecraft/simulate_info/blocks/beetroots.json looks like:

{
    "age": {
        "advance_probability": {
            "value1": "super",
            "operator": "/",
            "value2": 3
        }
    }
}

Basically, this takes the SimulationMethod assigned to age on the beetroot block and only changes the advance_probability field while keeping the rest the same. The rest is defined in minecraft/simulate_info/tags/crops.json, which gets applied to all blocks with the crops tag.

Now, if a mod wanted to change the behaviour of all crops so that it'd only grow during a certain time of the day, they could make a file in minecraft/simulate_info/tags/crops.json and do something like this:

{
    "priority": 999, // Make sure this gets applied AFTER Unloaded Activity applies its SimulationData.
    "age": {
        "advance_probability": {
            "predicate": {
                "check": "current_time",
                "comparison": "less_than",
                "value": 12000
            },
            "success": "super",
            "fail": 0
        }
    }
}

So instead of writing "unloadedactivity:property", you can just write "property". advance_probability UpdatingValueExpression The probability of the SimulationMethod performing 1 successful step per random/precipitation tick. A "step" can mean different things depending on the SimulationMethod. String[] The keys to different SimulationMethods on the same block that needs to have been finished before this SimulationMethod can start. docs.title: What is a SimulationData?
docs.text: A SimulationData holds all the SimulationMethods for a specific block. A block can only have one SimulationData assigned to it, but if several datapacks/mods tries to assign a SimulationData to the same block, or if a datapack/mod has assigned a SimulationData to a block and a tag which the block is assigned to, it will merge the data and end up with just one SimulationData.

docs.title: How to assign SimulationDatas to blocks/tags
docs.text:
Firstly, create a json file for your block/tag in your datapack/resources folder. For blocks the path will be data/<namespace>/simulate_info/blocks/<block_name>.json, and for tags the path will be data/<namespace>/simulate_info/tags/<tag_name>.json.

For example, the minecraft:beetroots block will be in data/minecraft/simulate_info/blocks/beetroots.json, and the minecraft:crops tag will be in data/minecraft/simulate_info/tags/crops.json.

Inside these files is where you define your SimulationData. Here's an example: 

{
    "priority": 999, // Optional. Default value is 1000
    "replace": true, // Optional. Default value is false
    "custom_key_name": {  /* Define SimulationMethod properties here */ },
    "the_key_can_be_anything": { /* Define SimulationMethod properties here */ },
    "except_for_priority_and_replace": { /* Define SimulationMethod properties here */ }
}

docs.title: SimulationData properties
docs.text: Field Type Description priority? Number The priority the entry. Lower values will be applied later, and higher values will be applied earlier. Entries on blocks will always be applied after entries on tags, no matter the priority. (Default: 1000) replace? Boolean If it should discard all old data and start fresh. By default, if there's 2 different entries affecting the same block, the one with lower priority will overlay it's data on top of the previous entry. (Default: false) . . . SimulationMethod Any other field that isn't priority or replace should have a SimulationMethod. The field name may be used to identify the SimulationMethod from other SimulationMethods, or to modify/override it from other entries.

docs.title: Simple merging
docs.text:
If you got the following SimulationData definition on the same block: 

{
    "method1": {  /* Define SimulationMethod properties here */ }
}

{
    "method2": {  /* Define SimulationMethod properties here */ }
}
The final SimulationData for that block will look like this:

{
    "method1": {  /* Define SimulationMethod properties here */ },
    "method2": {  /* Define SimulationMethod properties here */ }
}

docs.title: Overriding methods
docs.text:
If you now got these following SimulationData definition on the same block: 

{
    "old_method": {  /* Define SimulationMethod properties here */ }
}

{
    "priority": 999,
    "replace": true,
    "new_method": {  /* Define SimulationMethod properties here */ }
}
The final SimulationData for that block will look like this:

{
    "new_method": {  /* Define SimulationMethod properties here */ }
}
This is because lower priority gets applied later, and because replace was set to true, it cleared out any old SimulationData for that block.

docs.title: Overriding fields
docs.text:
If you now got these following SimulationData definition on the same block: 

{
    "method": {
        "value": "hello",
        "other_value": 5
    }
}

{
    "priority": 999,
    "method": {
        "value": "world"
    }
}
The final SimulationData for that block will look like this:

{
    "method": {
        "value": "world",
        "other_value": 5
    }
}
This is because lower priority gets applied later, and any fields that gets defined overriddes the old data, unless it's a JSON object or Array. Then the fields/elements gets merged.

docs.title: What is a SimulationMethod?
docs.text: A SimulationMethod is a way of simulating a block. For example, "unloadedactivity:property" simulates increasing a property value of a block, and "unloadedactivity:replace" simulates replacing a block with another.

docs.title: How to assign SimulationMethods to blocks/tags
docs.text:
In the file where you define your SimulationData, you can add your SimulationMethods by creating a field with any name except for "priority" and "replace" and then defining it there.

The "simulation_method" field must be set to a valid SimulationMethod Identifier. To see all available SimulationMethods and their Identifier, see the pages underneath For Developers>Available SimulationMethods.

Here's an example from the sweet berry bush: 

{
    "age": {
        "simulation_method": "property",
        "property_name": "age",
        "update_type": "update_clients",

        "conditions": [
            {
                "check": "raw_brightness_above",
                "comparison": "greater_or_equal",
                "value": 9
            }
        ],

        "advance_probability": 0.2
    }
}
It creates a SimulationMethod with the key "age" with the SimulationMethod "unloadedactivity:property".

You can have several SimulationMethods in one SimulationData, and they don't have to be defined in the same file. If you assign one SimulationMethod to a tag and one to a block which has that tag, that block will have both SimulationMethods. But if they have the same key, one SimulationMethod is gonna merge its data with the other SimulationMethod.

docs.title: What are ValueExpressions?
docs.text: ValueExpressions are values that gets evaluated when simulating. When they get evaluated, they have information about the world and the block it's simulating, so it's able to return different values based on the context.

docs.title: ValueExpression containers
docs.text: There are different types of containers for ValueExpressions. There is FixedExpression, UpdatingExpression and RandomizedExpression.

docs.title: FixedExpression
docs.text: The ValueExpression may only get affected stuff that doesn't change over time or isn't random. For example, surrounding blocks or block brightness. Something like local brightness would not be valid because that changes based on the time of day. If you try to create a FixedExpression with a ValueExpression that doesn't meet the requirements, an error will be thrown.

docs.title: UpdatingExpression
docs.text: The ValueExpression may only get affected stuff that is predictable. So anything that isn't random. If you try to create a FixedExpression with a ValueExpression that doesn't meet the requirements, an error will be thrown.

docs.title: RandomizedExpression
docs.text: Anything goes

Cannot be assigned

This SimulationMethod is abstract. This is what every other SimulationMethod builds upon.

This SimulationMethod allows blocks to simulate together at the same time. This is needed for simulating stuff like ice freezing, or grass growing, where it only grows from the edges and slowly grows inwards. If you want to use this, you may want to look at how to create a GroupInfo.

docs.title: Implementation Details
docs.text:
When using this SimulationMethod, it is gonna increase the value of the target property. It will use the property whose name matches what you set in the property_name field. If the property is an IntegerProperty, it will increase it for every successful trial. If it's a BooleanProperty, there will only be a maximum of 1 successful trial, which will turn its value from false to true.

Implements Value Description Method identifier unloadedactivity:property Set the simulation_method property to "unloadedactivity:property" or just "property" to use this SimulationMethod. Dependable? ✅ You are able to use this SimulationMethod as a dependency on another SimulationMethod. Groupable? ✅ You are able to use this SimulationMethod inside of group simulations.

docs.title: Blacklisting blocks
docs.text: Sometimes, Unloaded Activity will not properly simulate certain blocks. Especially modded blocks. One thing you can do in the meantime while the bug is getting fixed is to blacklist the blocks.

docs.title: Adding/Removing blocks to the blacklist
docs.text: There are 2 ways to add blocks to the blacklist:

docs.title: Config file
docs.text:
The config file can be found over at config/unloadedactivity.json in your Minecraft/server directory. Inside, there's a list assigned to blacklistedBlocks, and you simply add your block or block tag to that list.

Example:

{
    ...
    "blacklistedBlocks": [
        "minecraft:grass_block",
        "#minecraft:crops"
    ],
    ...
}

docs.title: In-game
docs.text:
To add a block or block tag to the blacklist in-game, you can use this command: /unloadedactivity config blacklistedBlocks add

To remove a block/tag, you use this command: /unloadedactivity config blacklistedBlocks remove

To list all currently blacklisted blocks, use this command: /unloadedactivity config blacklistedBlocks list

docs.title: Config options
docs.text: Config options can be found over at config/unloadedactivity.json in your Minecraft/server directory. If you don't wanna have to navigate your files to change the config options, they can also be changed in-game using /unloadedactivity config. (You will need to be in single player or have OP level 4)

docs.title: enableSimulatingBlockEntities
docs.text:
Default value: true

If Unloaded Activity should perform simulations for block entities.

docs.title: simulateFurnaceSmelting
docs.text:
Default value: true

If Unloaded Activity should simulate furnaces smelting items.

docs.title: blacklistedBlocks
docs.text:
Default value: []

A list of blocks that will not be simulated. See Blacklisting blocks for more info.

docs.title: enableSimulatingPrecipitationTicks
docs.text:
Default value: true

If Unloaded Activity should perform simulations marked as a precipitation tick simulation.

docs.title: enableSimulatingRandomTicks
docs.text:
Default value: true

If Unloaded Activity should perform simulations marked as a random tick simulation.

docs.title: maxChunkUpdatesPerTick
docs.text:
Default value: 24

Controls how many chunks Unloaded Activity is allowed to simulate per tick.

This does not apply for grouped simulations. For that, you have to change maxGroupTickSize.

docs.title: maxChunksIndexedPerTick
docs.text:
Default value: 4

Controls how many chunks Unloaded Activity is allowed to index per tick.

docs.title: multiplyMaxChunkUpdatesPerPlayer
docs.text:
Default value: false

If Unloaded Activity should multiply maxChunkUpdatesPerTick amount my the amount of players.

docs.title: multiplyMaxChunksIndexedPerPlayer
docs.text:
Default value: false

If Unloaded Activity should multiply maxChunksIndexedPerTick amount my the amount of players.

docs.title: randomizeBlockUpdates
docs.text:
Default value: false

Randomized the order in which blocks are simulated.

docs.title: enableSimulatingEntities
docs.text:
Default value: true

If Unloaded Activity should perform simulations for entities.

docs.title: simulateEntitiesAgeing
docs.text:
Default value: true

If Unloaded Activity should simulate baby mobs growing into adult mobs.

docs.title: simulateSheepDesireToEat
docs.text:
Default value: true

If Unloaded Activity should simulate trimmed sheep wanting to eat grass.

docs.title: convertCCAData
docs.text:
Default value: true

If set to true, it will convert the old Cardinal Components Api data that Unloaded Activity was using prior to v0.5.0 into the new data.

docs.title: debugLogs
docs.text:
Default value: false

Logs info to the console if set to true.

docs.title: fallbackToOverworldTime
docs.text:
Default value: true

This option is only for Minecraft 26.1 and above.

Versions below 26.1 will have the same behavior as if this value was set to true.

This option makes it so dimensions with no clock assigned to them will use the overworld time. In vanilla Minecraft, these dimensions are The Nether and The End.

If this is set to false, those dimensions will not be simulated, unless you use useSystemTime.

docs.title: tickDifferenceThreshold
docs.text:
Default value: 100

Determines how much of a time jump (in ticks) needs to occur before Unloaded Activity simulation happens.

docs.title: unloadedSimulationSpeed
docs.text:
Default value: 1.0

Determines the speed of Unloaded Activity's simulations. For example, values below 1.0 will make crops grow less, and values above 1.0 will make crops grow more.

docs.title: useSystemTime
docs.text:
Default value: false

Determines if Unloaded Activity should use the system time or game time for simulations. If this option is set to true, Unloaded Activity will now also simulate blocks if the game is paused for a while, or if the server is closed for a while.

A side effect of using this option is that sleeping to skip the night will not work. This is because Unloaded Activity will not see a big jump between the current time and the last time something was simulated.

docs.title: enableSimulatingGroups
docs.text:
Default value: true

If Unloaded Activity should perform simulations that are part of a simulation group.

docs.title: groupTickDifferenceThreshold
docs.text:
Default value: 1000

Determines how much of a time jump (in ticks) needs to occur before Unloaded Activity simulates a group.

docs.title: groupTickUpdateStrength
docs.text:
Default value: 1.0

How big the iteration steps should be. Smaller steps are more accurate but can reduce performance. The iteration size will be capped depending on what's being simulated and what value maxGroupTickIterations and minGroupTickIterations are set to.

docs.title: maxForcedChunkLoads
docs.text:
Default value: 0

If a group simulation ends up spreading to unloaded chunks, this will determine how many chunks Unloaded Activity is allowed to load.

docs.title: maxGroupTickDeviationScale
docs.text:
Default value: 0.1

How much the tick difference from a nearby chunk can deviate from to the main chunk when doing grouped simulations.

docs.title: maxGroupTickIterations
docs.text:
Default value: 128

How many iterations Unloaded Activity is allowed to do when doing group simulations.

Unloaded Activity may do different amounts of iterations based on the blocks simulation probability and the amount of time passed, but it will never exceed this value.

docs.title: maxGroupTickSize
docs.text:
Default value: 2500

How many blocks a group simulation can simulate.

Some simulation groups are more expensive to simulate. Those groups will reduce the total amount be a custom percentage. Different simulation groups may not always allow the same amount of blocks.

docs.title: maxGroupUpdatesPerTick
docs.text:
Default value: 1

The amount of group simulations Unloaded Activity is allowed to do per tick. Group simulations are quite expensive, so this value should generally be kept low.

docs.title: minGroupTickIterations
docs.text:
Default value: 8

Minimum amount of iterations Unloaded Activity should try to do when doing group simulations.

Unloaded Activity may do different amounts of iterations based on the blocks simulation probability and the amount of time passed, but sometimes it does too few iterations and the result won't be accurate.
